text: FBI most-wanted cartel boss captured; gunfire at stadium sparks panic - video. A Mexican drug cartel leader listed among the FBI’s 10 most wanted fugitives has reportedly been captured by the country’s military, triggering violent exchanges of gunfire in Sinaloa state that sent baseball fans fleeing from a stadium during a match on Friday. Multiple Mexican media outlets reported the arrest of Fausto Isidro Meza-Flores, known as “El Chapo Isidro”, who allegedly heads the Meza-Flores Transnational Criminal Organisation, also known as Los Mazatlecos. US Media outlet CNN said it was seeking independent confirmation from Mexican authorities and that the arrest had not been officially verified. The reported operation took place in Guasave, a city in Sinaloa known for its agricultural activity. Local authorities confirmed “an attack on federal personnel” in the city, according to CNN. The footage showed Mexican security force helicopters firing towards the ground while circling over Guasave. Gunfire also disrupted a baseball match at Kuroda Park stadium, where spectators were seen scrambling out of the stands. People could be heard shouting, “Get down, duck down, down, down!” as fans climbed over barriers. An official broadcast showed players from Venados de Mazatlán and Algodoneros de Guasave leaving the field midway through the game. “It’s being suspended… there’s a situation happening off the field,” the announcers said during the broadcast. “We wish first and foremost to ask God that everything is OK… there is a national security incident, it may be better for us to go to break now.” The FBI lists Meza-Flores as an alleged leader of a heavily armed drug-trafficking organisation based in Sinaloa. Its wanted notice accuses him and his network of trafficking heroin, methamphetamine, cocaine, fentanyl and marijuana into the United States. The US government is offering a reward of up to $5 million for information leading to his arrest or conviction. “Known as El Chapo Isidro, he’s accused of spending the last 20 years flooding the U.S. with fentanyl, cocaine, heroin, and other deadly drugs, first as an independent drug trafficker and later as the head of the Meza-Flores cartel,” Acting FBI Director Driscoll said. Driscoll added that the organisation was also accused of crimes “ranging from kidnapping and extortion to torture and murder”. Meza-Flores was first indicted in a US federal court in 2012. A superseding indictment and arrest warrant were issued on November 26, 2019, charging him with multiple drug-trafficking violations and firearm possession.
